overall_design_parameters.quote: (1) Overall total pressure ratio ≈ 3.0 (average stage pressure ratio ≈ 1.44) (2) Equivalent specific weight flow ≈ 30 lb/sec/sq ft frontal area (inlet axial Mach number = 0.555) (3) Tip speed = 1,200 ft/sec (4) Inlet hub-tip ratio = 0.50 (5) Exit hub-tip ratio = 0.75 (6) Constant tip diameter = 16 inches (7) Ratio of discharge axial velocity to inlet axial velocity ≈ 0.75

no_igv.quote: No inlet guide vanes were used in the compressor design.

design_specific_weight_flow.quote: A tip relative inlet Mach number of 1.24 was arbitrarily selected for the first rotor. This Mach number combined with a tip speed of 1,200 ft/sec resulted in a design specific weight flow of 29.8 pounds per second per square foot of frontal area.

design_point_summary.quote: stagnation pressure ratio of 2.96 (an average stagnation pressure ratio per stage of 1.44) with a corrected specific weight flow of 29.8 pounds per

test_medium.quote: formance was obtained from tests of the compressor in Freon-12 at corrected speeds from 40 to 100 percent of the Freon equivalent of the [design speed]

freon_equivalence_definition.value: Freon equivalent condition: rotational speed and weight flow in Freon giving the same mean-radius rotor relative inlet Mach number and inlet angle as the air design values (method of ref. 14)
freon_equivalence_definition.quote: The Freon equivalent condition corresponding to any air design condition is the combination of rotational speed and weight flow in Freon which makes the mean radius section rotor relative inlet Mach number and the inlet angle the same as the corresponding air design values.

clearance_design.quote: Rotor tip and stator hub clearances of 0.030 inch were used as design values. A check of the unit indicated that rotor tip clearances were generally close to design values but that the stator hub clearances were greater and nonuniform.

stator_hub_clearance_measured.quote: The following are clearances measured for the two blades in each stator row located on either side of one-half of the split stator casing: [table Stator / Clearance, inches Left side Right side / Clearance, percent average span Left side Right side] ... The clearances are considered to be typical of each stator row.

profiles.value: NACA 65-series thickness with trailing-edge region thickened to TE radius = 10 percent of max thickness, all blading; rotor 1: A2I8b mean line 6% t/c at tip, A6I4b 8% at mean, A10 10% at hub; stators A10 mean line; stators 1, 2 t/c linear 6 to 10% hub to tip, stator 3 6 to 9.6%
profiles.quote: the A2I8b mean line (ref. 12) was used at the tip section of the first rotor and the tip maximum thickness was chosen to be 6 percent of the chord length ... the A10 mean line was used at the hub. The hub maximum blade thickness ... was selected to be 10 percent. ... the A6I4b mean line was used at the mean radius. The maximum thickness at the mean radius was 8 percent. ... The maximum thickness for both first and second stators varied linearly from 6 to 10 percent from hub to tip. Maximum thickness for the third stator varied linearly from 6 to 9.6 from hub to tip. The NACA 65-series thickness distribution, with a trailing-edge region thickened to a trailing-edge radius equal to 10 percent of the maximum thickness, was used for all blading.

rotor_masters.value: all three rotors from one master by cutting off the tip section; stators 2 and 3 from one master by cutting off the tip
rotor_masters.quote: It was possible to fabricate all three rotors from the same master by cutting off the tip section for the shorter rotor blades. Stators 2 and 3 were fabricated from one master by cutting off the tip (the tip being at the outer casing) for the shorter blades.

stator1_fabrication_error.value: hub and tip blade settings of stator 1 interchanged (gives large Δα' values in Table III)
stator1_fabrication_error.quote: The moderately large Δα' values for stator 1 resulted from a fabrication error in which the hub and tip blade settings were interchanged.

delta_definitions.value: Δα' = α' at design minus αd from low-speed cascade tests (equivalent velocity diagrams); Δα = actual angle of attack minus low-speed cascade design angle of attack; Δθ' = actual minus required equivalent design turning angle
delta_definitions.quote: The differences between α' used at design conditions and the αd as obtained from low-speed cascade tests are tabulated in table III as Δα' ... The resulting differences between actual angles of attack and low-speed cascade design angles of attack are indicated as Δα in table III.

section_radius_and_solidity_basis.value: profiles applied at the average of inlet and exit radii of each conical surface; solidities computed at these average radii
section_radius_and_solidity_basis.quote: To facilitate blade fabrication all blade section profiles were applied at the average of the inlet and exit radii for each conical surface. Blade element solidities were calculated using these average radii for each conical surface.

stream_surfaces.value: conical surfaces keeping the ratio of radial distance between streamlines to passage height constant at row inlet and exit
stream_surfaces.quote: All blade row calculations were made assuming that the flow across each row occurred along conical surfaces generated by maintaining the ratio of radial distance between streamlines to radial passage height constant at the inlet and exit of the row.

rotor_materials.value: rotor blades duraluminum, unpolished (groove-to-ridge 0.0019 in., ridge spacing 0.044 in.); stator blades cast fiberglas and paraplex
rotor_materials.quote: 0.0019 inch and the distance between ridges was 0.044 inch. The rotor blades were used in the unpolished state.
